entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This reference under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter called as LA Act), was sent to the reference court by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred as LAC).
2.

As per the LAC Award, a large tract of land measuring 1074 Bigha of village Pooth Khurd, Delhi, was acquired by the Govt. for a public purpose namely "Rohini Residential Scheme, under Planned Development of Delhi".
Notification under Section 4 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act') was issued on 21-03-2003.
Declaration under Section 6 was made on 19-03-2004.

Thereafter, Award bearing no.
07/2005-06/DC(NW) was announced by Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as LAC) on 12-07-2005.

The LAC determined the market price of the acquired land as Rs.15,70,000/-
per acre for land falling in Category 'A' LAC No. 119/22 page 2 of 9 and Rs.14,00,000/- per acre for land falling in 'B' Category.
3.
The petitioner being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC, filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The Land Acquisition Collector forwarded the same to this court, for adjudication.

4. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are that petitioner was the owner/bhumidar as well as in the actual, physical and cultivatory possession of the land bearing khasra numbers as mentioned in the statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/denial of documents, situated within the Revenue Estate of Village Pooth Khurd, Delhi (the said land).

The said land was acquired vide notification dated 21.03.2003.
5.

The case of the petitioner can be summed up by stating that the award was bad due to inadequacy of compensation and incorrect assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non-consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land, the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market LAC No. 119/22 page 3 of 9 value of the adjoining areas/villages, the sale deeds of other lands of the contemporary period, nearness to the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.

6. The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced rate besides interest thereon and solatium in addition to the compensation.
7.
The respondent no.1/the Union of India (UOI)/ Land Acquisition Collector contested the reference petition by filing written statement.

However, respondent no.2/Delhi Development Authority (DDA) adopted the WS filed on behalf of R-1/UOI.
8.

The petition has been contested mainly on the ground that the LAC awarded adequate compensation to the petitioner after taking into consideration all the relevant factors and therefore,
LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land after taking into account the market rates Mandir Shri Radha Krishna vs Union Of India And Anr (07/05-06 Pooth ... on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24740656/
2 prevailing at the time of notification under Section 4 of LA Act.

sentences.text: 9. During admission-denial of documents, the counsel for petitioner admitted the statement given u/s 19 of the Act.

The following issues were framed:-
i) Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement LAC No. 119/22 page 4 of 9 in compensation, if so, to what amount?
ii) Relief.
10. In evidence, the petitioner has relied upon the judgment in a case Randhir Singh Vs. Union of India & Ors., and also the evidence led in said case.

entities.text: Randhir Singh Vs. Union of India & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. The respondent no.1/Union of India, in its evidence, tendered the award as Ex. R1.
The respondent no. 2/DDA adopted the evidence led on behalf of the respondent no.1/ Union of India.
12. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.

My issue-wise findings are given as under:-
FINDINGS ON ISSUE NO. 1 :-
13.
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to show as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.

During arguments, Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgments titled as Randhir Singh vs. UOI, LA No.1469/16 decided on 10.08.2018 by Learned Predecessor Sh. Neeraj Gaur, ld. ADJ-01 as well as Narain Singh Dabas vs. UOI LAC No.51/2019 decided on LAC No. 119/22 page 5 of 9 10.01.2023 by Undersigned cases and conceded that award be passed in terms of the said judgments and the same enhancement which was granted in the said judgments be also granted to petitioner.

entities.text: Randhir Singh vs. UOI, LA No.1469/16
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Narain Singh Dabas vs. UOI LAC No.51/2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. In the aforesaid case, Ld. Predecessor had adjudicated the market value of Category A land of village Pooth Khurd acquired through award No.7/2005- 06 as Rs.19,80,750/- per acre.
The petitioner is accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land of Category A as was awarded in Randhir Singh's case.
I accordingly adjudicate the market value of Category A land of the petitioner as Rs.19,80,750/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,10,750/- per acre is accorded.

15. As far as land of Category B is concerned, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in a case titled as Jai Singh Vs. UOI, LA No.266/08, decided on 23.08.2011 (Delhi High Court) had adopted/used a formula for determination of fair market value of Category B land vis-a-vis land of Category 'A'.

entities.text: Jai Singh Vs. UOI, LA No.266/08
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Jai Singh's case fair market value of Category B land was adjudicated to be 2.5% less than fair market value of Category A land.

It is a matter of record that the land of Village Pooth Khurd was in Mandir Shri Radha Krishna vs Union Of India And Anr (07/05-06 Pooth ... on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24740656/
3 consideration before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi while deciding Jai LAC No. 119/22 page 6 of 9 Singh's case (Supra).

entities.text: Mandir Shri Radha Krishna vs Union Of India And Anr (07/05-06 Pooth
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, I find no impediment in adopting/relying upon the formula adopted by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in said case.
In fact this court is under an obligation/duty to follow the orders passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi as well as Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

On applying the formula adopted/used by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Jai Singh's case (Supra) the fair market value of category B land of village Pooth Khurd acquired by same Notification is calculated to be 2.5% lesser than the market value of category A land.
Hence, the market value of category B land of Village Pooth Khurd acquired by same Notification is adjudicated to be Rs.19,31,231/- per acre.

16. Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12%
additional amount [as per Section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)] and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
17. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF LAC No. 119/22 page 7 of 9

The share(s) of the petitioner(s) would be determinable as per the statement u/s 19 of the L.A.
Act LAC No. 119/22 page 8 of 9 proved on record and the said statement shall constitute a part of this award.
19.
Reference petition stands answered.
Parties to bear their own costs.
A copy of this award be sent to the LAC for necessary information, action and expeditious compliance for remittance of the amount.
File be consigned to record room.
